text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 4

The panel composition points nowhere useful: you and the appointee are both women, so sex-based preference can't explain why she was chosen over you. Raising it would read as grasping and would undercut the part of your case that is genuinely strong.

That stronger case is qualifications. On the published facts you hold a master's in educational leadership and five years of actual leadership practice; she holds unspecified "courses." Where appointments must go to the most qualified applicant, that gap is the argument.

Act on the silence instead. Send a written follow-up citing your original date and any statutory deadline for reasons, and ask for the panel's assessment criteria and scoring. Without their stated reasoning you can't evaluate anything — including whether something improper occurred.
